text:
maria-customer: Hi team — getting consistent 401 invalid_api_key when our backend uploads files to the Redwood API behind our nginx reverse proxy. Works fine from my laptop curl but our server fails. Response: `{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"401\"}`

anna-support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the raw request headers and the exact curl or client command you're using? Also does the server use chunked transfer (Transfer-Encoding: chunked)?

maria-customer: Repro steps: from the server we do `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" -F file=@payload.bin https://api.redwood.example/v1/upload`
Server request dump (from our proxy access log):
```
POST /v1/upload HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
User-Agent: our-uploader/1.2
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary

<chunked body>...
```
Response from Redwood: `401 invalid_api_key`

matt-eng: Thanks @maria-customer. Two quick asks: 1) can you capture a raw request (tcpdump or nginx proxy_pass access echo) that shows what gets forwarded to Redwood? 2) confirm whether the Authorization header is present in the proxied request or if it's only present in the client->proxy leg. Some proxies will fold headers if chunked encoding and multipart boundaries are weird.

maria-customer: I grabbed an upstream (nginx) proxy log — looks like nginx forwards the request but the `Authorization` header is only present in the first TCP segment. Upstream debug (nginx error_log set to debug):
```
proxy_set_header Authorization -> "Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED"
proxy_pass to 10.0.5.12:443
client sent chunked body, proxy buffered chunked body to temp file
forwarding headers: Host, User-Agent, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding
(not listing Authorization?)
```
I'm seeing the header in the access_log on ingress but not in the egress to Redwood.

anna-support: Interesting — two possibilities: 1) proxy config drops Authorization when buffering chunked bodies to disk (rare), or 2) our SDK/client is using `Expect: 100-continue` or some streaming that splits the header into an initial request that the proxy treats differently. Can you try forcing a Content-Length (disable chunked) as a quick test? e.g. `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" --data-binary @payload.bin --header "Content-Length: $(stat -c%s payload.bin)" https://api.redwood.example/v1/upload`

maria-customer: Quick test: when I add Content-Length it's accepted (200). When using chunked it fails (401). So workaround ok but not great for large/streaming uploads.

matt-eng: Thanks. This looks like an interoperability bug between nginx's buffering and certain client libraries that send Transfer-Encoding: chunked and then rely on the proxy to forward Authorization. We saw one internally in Node SDK v0.8.2 where node-fetch/undici can trigger chunked uploads and some older proxy configs drop sensitive headers when request body is buffered. Two action items: 1) short-term — rotate the key and issue a new key scoped for uploads (we can do a one-off) and ask you to use Content-Length or chunking-safe proxy config; 2) long-term — engineering to add a server-side tolerance check and better rejection message to avoid confusing `invalid_api_key` vs header-drop (and visible tracing).

anna-support: @matt-eng can you confirm if we have server-side logs showing `missing Authorization` vs `invalid key` for trace id X-Req-ID: abc123 (maria attached trace id in headers)?

maria-customer: Attached request/response pair shows `x-request-id: abc123` in our ingress; response included `x-rw-trace: abc123` and body `{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\"}`.

matt-eng: I pulled the logs for x-rw-trace=abc123 — our edge logs show the request arrived *without* Authorization and was rejected by auth middleware (hence invalid_api_key). So root cause confirmed: header not forwarded. We'll escalate to infra to audit nginx buffering behavior.

ops-oncall: Created INC-4628: "nginx buffering drops Authorization header when Transfer-Encoding: chunked" — priority P2. Escalating to eng-infra.

incident-bot: Ticket INC-4628 created by ops-oncall — https://redwood.incidents/INC-4628 :eyes:

anna-support: Summary / recommended next steps for @maria-customer: 1) rotate the affected API key (we can issue a scoped upload key) — we recommend rotate now and revoke old key once you confirm the workaround. 2) short-term workaround: ensure client sets Content-Length or stream via a chunking-safe path (bypass buffering) 3) we'll follow up from eng-infra on a config/compat doc and track INC-4628 for a permanent mitigation. If you want us to rotate the key now say `please rotate` and we'll do it. :thumbsup:
